\begin{abstract}
This supplement collects the Santander tables and figure, the MULAN selection rule, the implementation survey, the leaf-saturation checks, the synthetic study and the full MULAN dose-response table that the main text summarizes. Every number is a macro generated by \texttt{make\_tables.py} from the released result files; \texttt{release/REPRODUCE.md} maps each item to its result file and to the command that regenerates it.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle

\section{Santander: figure and additional tables}
\label{app:santander}
\begin{figure*}[H]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=.85\textwidth]{figures/fig2_shift_vs_lnw.pdf}
\Description{Two scatter plots over the 24 Santander labels. Left: the realized per-label logit shift against the intended shift ln w. The five labels with no saturated cell sit on the identity line; the other nineteen are drawn as triangles at the top, marking that their shift is not identifiable. Right: the share of saturated cells against ln w, showing that every one of those nineteen has saturated cells.}
\caption{\textbf{Elkan's shift holds exactly where the learner does not saturate and breaks where it does.} \textbf{A.} For each Santander label, the intended shift $\ln w_j$ against the label-free prevalence-matching shift $b_j$ of \Sm (the constant that returns the mean prediction to the training prevalence); the dashed line is $b_j=\ln w_j$, the behaviour Proposition~1 of the main text predicts. The \nSnIdentShift{} labels with no saturated cell lie on the line. On the other \nnCappedShift{} (triangles) $b_j$ is not identified at all: a cell at exactly $1.0$ cannot be moved by any finite shift, so it contributes a constant whatever $b$ is and the bisection settles near its bound. Those labels are drawn at the bound rather than at a value, because the value would be the clipping constant and not a property of the learner. \textbf{B.} Share of test cells at exactly $1.0$ per label against $\ln w_j$. Santander, \nnLabels{} labels, \nnTest{} test rows.}
\label{fig:two}
\end{figure*}
\begin{table}[H]
\caption{Repair ladder on Santander ($\mapseven$, test-split protocol, 70\% evaluation split; the ceiling row is fitted and evaluated on all test rows and differs from the split by less than $0.001$). \Sm and \Nm are the same LightGBM configuration with and without per-label weights; \Wm is Wasserstein gradient boosting (direct probabilities, no weights). ``Dead'' = label without positives in the calibration split; identity keeps its raw score, prior replaces it by the training prevalence, excluded removes it from the candidate set. Bold = the recommended prior policy (exclusion is equal or slightly better). The per-label isotonic family is the best repair on every model under either explicit dead-label policy, exclusion running a little above prior throughout; prior is the recommended default because it keeps the label in the candidate set. an intercept-only per-label shift already recovers most of the weighted model's loss; the shared map changes the weighted model only through ties (cells at exactly $1.0$ or $0.0$); the weighted model's in-sample ceiling stays below the unweighted raw score. Saturation shares are exact-value counts over all test cells; the within-label AUC is invariant to any per-label monotone map.}
\label{tab:ladder}

\section{Selection rule on MULAN}
\label{app:tau}
\Cref{tab:tau} reports the cross-validated selection for the default LightGBM at $w{=}1$; the result file covers all \nnTauCells{} learner--dataset cells. The rule ends more than $0.01$ below raw in \nnTauSelBelowRaw{} of them (\ntauFailCells): in each, the out-of-fold ranking of the candidates on the calibration split does not carry over to the standard test file of the benchmark, so the failure is one of the split, not of the rule.
\begin{table*}[p]
\caption{Cross-validated selection on MULAN, default LightGBM, $w{=}1$ ($\mathrm{MAP}@\min(7,L)$ on the standard test split). Candidates: per-label isotonic with prior fallback at positives threshold $\tau\in\{\ntauList\}$, the shared map, and no calibration (raw); \ntauFolds-fold cross-validation inside the calibration split picks the candidate with the best out-of-fold $\mapk$. Columns: calibration rows, test rows, raw, per-label isotonic at $\tau=0$ and its paired bootstrap difference to raw ($B=\ntauBootB$, 95\% interval), the selected candidate, its test $\mapk$ and paired difference to raw (``--'' when raw itself is selected), and the shared map. The selection removes every interval-significant loss (\nnHurtAfterTau{} of \nnMulan) and produces an interval-significant gain on \nnTauSigGain{} of \nnMulan, delicious ($\ndelCiTauSel$ at $\tau=\ndelTauSel$), the dataset with the most labels; it never used test labels.}
\label{tab:tau}
\footnotesize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}

\section{Calibrators on a single-class calibration window}

\Cref{tab:survey} summarizes the implementation survey behind Remark~2 of the main text (versions, file names and line numbers are in the repository file \texttt{docs/dead\_label\_survey.md}). ``Constant'' means the calibrator returns a constant for a label whose calibration window has one class; ``raises'' means it refuses; ``identity'' means the raw score is returned; ``n/a'' means no per-label calibration is offered.

\section{Synthetic study with known marginals}
\label{app:synthetic}
\Cref{tab:synthetic} lists every cell of the synthetic study (settings in the caption); the text of Section~4 of the main text quotes the $D=3$, $e=1$ rows.
\begin{table*}[p]
\caption{Synthetic multi-label data with known marginals ($L=\nsynL$, $n=\nsynN$ rows for training and test, \nsynSeeds{} seeds, $\mathrm{MAP}@\nsynK$). Prevalences span $10^{-D}$ to $0.3$; weights are $w_j=r_j^{e}$. Ranking by the true marginals is the Bayes optimum. Logistic regression is the realizable learner; LGBM-S is LightGBM with 30 trees and 4 leaves, LGBM-L with 300 trees and 31 leaves; XGBoost (200 trees, depth 5) and a two-layer MLP are the other learners. Both LightGBM sizes fail to invert once cells saturate; XGBoost saturates nothing and inverts. Where the inversion fails, the realized shift is no longer the constant $\ln w_j$ under which a per-label offset is Bayes-optimal~\cite{Wang2026BeyondLA}, but the distortion remains per-label monotone.}
\label{tab:synthetic}
\footnotesize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}rrrc|cc|cccr|cccr|cc|cc@{}}
\toprule
